gmm.modal.info.bugs.title: Report a Bug
gmm.modal.info.bugs.intro: If you've found a bug or have a feature request, please raise an issue on the project tracker.
gmm.modal.info.about.p.1: Welcome to Giffyglyph's Monster Maker Continued, by Skyl3lazer! This Foundry module pairs with GIFFYGLYPH'S MONSTER MAKER (PDF) to help you build monsters for D&D 5e real fast.
gmm.modal.info.about.p.2: If you like this module and want to see it grow, help out by becoming a patron or making a one-time donation.
gmm.modal.info.about.supportsubtitle: All of these links go to Giffyglyph, the original creator of this system and module.
gmm.modal.info.about.title: Giffyglyph's Monster Maker Continued
gmm.modal.info.about.subtitle: by Skyl3lazer
gmm.modal.info.deferral.title: Deferrals
gmm.modal.info.deferral.p.1: When using an uncommon or rare feature, you can use a deferral to change when it chooses targets, makes attacks, or applies effects. Use this to create ticking bombs, counterable regeneration effects, and give your players ways to avoid an incoming problem.
gmm.modal.info.deferral.p.2: There are two types of deferrals: delayed, which wait for a time before choosing targets and making attacks, and dooming, which attack immediately but leaves the effects for later once the target's doom clock runs out.
gmm.modal.info.deferral.p.3: {cancel} indicates what stops the deferred part from happening, such as a delayed area attack that has been avoided, or a doom the target manages to dispel.
gmm.modal.info.modifiers.li.1: Relative: Increase or decrease the automated value by an amount (i.e. av = av +/- x).
gmm.modal.info.modifiers.li.2: Absolute: Replace the automated value with a precise value (i.e. av = x).
gmm.modal.info.modifiers.p.1: To change an automated value (hit points, armor class, attack bonuses, etc), you can apply a positive or negative modifier.
gmm.modal.info.modifiers.p.2: There are two kinds of modifier:
gmm.modal.info.modifiers.title: Modifying Values
gmm.modal.info.modifying_abilities.p.1: To customise your monster's ability modifiers and saving throws, you can define a series of semi-colon-separated modifiers:
gmm.modal.info.modifying_abilities.p.2: These modifiers can be either relative or absolute. Use them to adjust (or replace) automated values where appropriate.
gmm.modal.info.modifying_abilities.title: Modifying Abilities
gmm.modal.info.ranked_abilities.p.1: Ability modifiers and saving throw values are automatically calculated based on your monster's level, rank, and role.
gmm.modal.info.ranked_abilities.p.2: To help prioritise certain aspects, rank the six abilities from the strongest (top) to the weakest (bottom).
gmm.modal.info.ranked_abilities.p.3: The higher an ability is ranked, the more influence it has on modifiers and saving throws.
gmm.modal.info.ranked_abilities.pre.1: e.g. STR, CON, CHA, WIS, INT, DEX
gmm.modal.info.ranked_abilities.title: Ranked Abilities
gmm.modal.info.scaling.title: Scaling Attacks
gmm.modal.info.scaling.p.1: When paired with a Giffyglyph monster, a scaling attack will automatically take into account the monster's proficiency bonus and the attack's relevant ability mod.
gmm.modal.info.scaling.p.2: Use these to easily create features and attacks that work at every monster level.
gmm.modal.info.shortcodes.title: Automated Shortcodes
gmm.modal.info.shortcodes.p.1: You can use shortcodes to automatically insert data from a parent monster. Note: this only occurs when the item is attached to a Giffyglyph monster.
gmm.modal.info.shortcodes.random.title: Randomized Dice Rolls
gmm.modal.info.shortcodes.random.p.1: Insert randomized dice rolls with a special shortcode. You can use any dice size, as shown below:
gmm.modal.info.shortcodes.list.title: Shortcodes
gmm.modal.info.shortcodes.list.p.1: Use shortcodes to pull data out of a Giffyglyph monster and insert it into your text.
gmm.modal.info.shortcodes.list.p.2: There are three save DCs: {saveDc} is the monster's stat-block DC. {featureDc} is the DC for this specific feature, which could potentially have changed from baseline. {durationSaveDc} is the DC of the recurring save that ends an ongoing effect, including any Save DC Modifier.
gmm.modal.info.shortcodes.modifiers.p.1: Use mathematical modifiers with your shortcodes to transform the final number and apply specific rounding. For example:
gmm.modal.info.shortcodes.modifiers.exam: The monster's save DC modified by their highest Mod
gmm.modal.info.shortcodes.dice.title: Shortcodes and Dice
gmm.modal.info.shortcodes.dice.p.1: Add a dice value to a shortcode to transform it into a dice roll. For example:
gmm.modal.info.shortcodes.dice.example.4: Attack Damage (shown in the default die for the monster)
gmm.modal.info.tags.p.1: Create tags to define categories and sub-types for your monster: ancestries, power sources, elements, factions, affiliations, etc.
gmm.modal.info.tags.p.2: You can create multiple tags at once by separating each tag with a semi-colon:
gmm.modal.info.tags.title: Monster Tags
gmm.modal.info.zone.title: Zones
gmm.modal.info.zone.p.1: A zone is an area that stays behind after the action is used and does something to the space it covers. Only an action that places an area can have a zone, so these controls appear once you pick a shape as the target.
gmm.modal.info.zone.p.2: Terrain Modifiers are what the space is for as long as the zone lasts: difficult ground, darkness, cover, and the rest of the pdf's Change Terrain list.
gmm.modal.info.zone.p.3: Zone Rules fire part of the action at whoever is in the area. Select the events when things happen, and choose what Fires: the action's damage, its attack roll, or the effects it applies. The zone does that thing instead, to whoever triggers it.
gmm.modal.info.zone.p.4: Applies to specifies who the zone affects. Once per Turn stops a creature that steps out and back in from being hit twice.
gmm.modal.info.zone.p.5: Automation will differ based on your available modules. Difficult ground and darkness need nothing beyond Foundry. Damage and attacks require Midi QOL, or Enhanced Region Behavior. A few of the book's modifiers don't have automation.

gmm.monster.artifact.legendary_actions.b: When another creature ends its turn, you can spend a number of legendary actions to perform one of the actions listed below. You regain spent legendary actions at the start of your turn.
gmm.monster.artifact.legendary_resistanc: When you would fail a saving throw, you can instead spend 1 legendary resistance to succeed at it. You regain spent legendary resistances when you finish a long rest.
gmm.monster.artifact.paragon_actions.blu: When another creature ends its turn, you can spend 1 paragon action to a) move or b) perform one action (attack, help, hide, etc). You regain spent paragon actions at the start of your turn.

gmm.effect.unsupported.blueprint: The blueprint is read before effects apply, so this will reach the sheet inconsistently or not at all.
gmm.effect.unsupported.hp_effective_max: It is re-derived from system.attributes.hp.max and system.attributes.hp.tempmax after effects apply; target one of those instead.
gmm.effect.unsupported.init_mod: The forge assigns it after effects apply. Target system.attributes.init.bonus instead.
gmm.effect.unsupported.init_prof: The forge assigns it after effects apply. A scaling monster adds no proficiency to initiative.
gmm.effect.unsupported.init_ability: The forge assigns it after effects apply. Set the initiative ability on the Forge sheet instead.
gmm.effect.unsupported.encumbrance: The forge assigns it after effects apply. Target system.abilities.str.value or the creature's size instead.
gmm.effect.unsupported.spellcasting: The forge assigns it after effects apply. Set the spellcasting ability on the Forge sheet instead.
gmm.effect.unsupported.spell_level: The forge assigns it after effects apply. Set the spellcasting level on the Forge sheet instead.
gmm.effect.unsupported.spell_dc: The forge assigns it after effects apply. Target system.bonuses.spell.dc instead.
gmm.effect.unsupported.ability_dc: The printed Spell DC is built from the blueprint and never reads this field. Target system.bonuses.spell.dc instead, which moves the row and the field.
gmm.effect.unsupported.skill_passive: The forge assigns it after effects apply; target {target} instead.

gmm.settings.track_paragon_actions.hint: Spend one of a scaling monster's paragon actions whenever it takes an action outside its own turn in combat, and refill the pool at the start of its turn. You'll get a warning if there are no actions left to spend.
gmm.settings.track_paragon_actions.name: Track Paragon Actions
gmm.settings.track_paragon_defenses.hint: Offer a scaling monster's paragon defenses on a failed saving throw, spending the hit point cost and one defense to turn the failure into a success. With MidiQOL you'll also get prompted for this use.
gmm.settings.track_paragon_defenses.name: Track Paragon Defenses
gmm.settings.automate_deferrals.hint: A delayed feature announces itself and starts a countdown on the monster instead of attacking. A dooming feature attacks at once, and each creature it hits carries a countdown of its own. The countdown ticks on the start of its bearer's turns, and at zero you are offered the feature's payload or the chance to call it off. Turn this off to resolve deferrals immediately and track the timer yourself. Requires Foundry v14.
gmm.settings.automate_deferrals.name: Automate Deferrals
gmm.settings.automate_durations.hint: An effect with a duration other than Instant is applied to its targets and carries the flags midi-qol and DAE need to run it. This includes the recurring saving throw of an Ongoing or Save Ends effect, and the reapplied damage of a Timed one. Turn this off to print the duration and track it yourself. Requires Foundry v14, and potentially other modules.
gmm.settings.automate_durations.name: Automate Durations
gmm.settings.deferral_countdown.name: Deferral Countdown
gmm.settings.deferral_countdown.hint: How a pending delayed or dooming countdown is drawn on the token carrying it, and on any area it placed.
gmm.settings.deferral_countdown.label: Customize Deferral Countdown
gmm.settings.deferral_countdown.title: Customize Deferral Countdown
Draw the remaining rounds as an overlay on the token, and in the middle of any area the feature placed.
gmm.settings.deferral_countdown.size.hin: A percentage of the smaller side of the token or area, so the number keeps its proportions.
gmm.settings.deferral_countdown.due_colo: Used once the countdown reaches zero but before the effects are applied.
